findings.title: The committed evaluation split has no held-out test set: every test trial is also a validation trial
findings.evidence: Cell 37 computes train_samples=floor(0.8*576)=460, testList=range(461,576) (115 indices), and train_test_split(X_train.indices_, test_size=0.2, shuffle=False) over range(576) gives val=460..575 (116 indices). Pure-Python re-derivation: test minus val = empty, val minus test = {460}, overlap = 115/115 = 100% of test. The line `train_set = windows_dataset` also discards splits['train'], so validation is carved from all 576 trials and the declared test set is scored on trials the model already validated on. Because cell 38 displays validation accuracy during model_option/training_percent selection, every test trial participates in selection.

findings.title: The only recorded result is exactly what a constant classifier scores on the recorded labels
findings.evidence: Cell 39 records 'Test acc: 24.35%'. On the 576 recorded labels from cell 32, always-predict-Neutral gives 115/460 = 25.00% (train), 29/116 = 25.00% (val) and 28/115 = 24.35% (test), reproducing the recorded 0.25 (cell 38 intrinsic summary: rows=100, std=0.0, min=max=0.25 for both train_accuracy and valid_accuracy) and 24.35% to the printed precision. The test slice's own majority is Disgust at 29/115 = 25.22%, so the pipeline scores below the trivial baseline; exact binomial p=0.2441 vs 0.20 and p=0.9146 vs 29/115, Wilson 95% CI [17.42%, 32.94%]. This is a quantitative identity about the recorded labels, not a claim about the model's internals or the published article.

findings.title: The recorded objective is not a valid NLL, so the loss curves cannot support any training claim
findings.evidence: Cell 37 passes criterion=torch.nn.NLLLoss while cell 35's committed torchsummary ends at Expression-18 with output [-1, 5] and lists no LogSoftmax/Softmax layer; a grep of all code cells finds no log_softmax/Softmax/CrossEntropy call. Cell 38's intrinsic summary records train_loss min -753759.28 / max -523.59 and valid_loss min -955689.18 / max -2314.25 over 100 epochs, all negative. A correct NLL over a normalised distribution is non-negative, so the recorded objective is inconsistent with the stated criterion. Reported as a separate finding, not folded into the split fix.

findings.title: The recorded epoch inputs cannot be regenerated by the committed preprocessing cells
findings.evidence: The committed score tables in cell 24 give 48 sessions with 7-15 score>=4 trials each (533 total; class counts Disgust 98, Fear 116, Sad 91, Neutral 134, Happy 94), and cell 30 filters on score>=4, so the committed pipeline would build 533 trials. Cells 31/32 instead record 12 events per file, 576 total (144/96/112/144/80), and cell 27's epochs.save is commented out. The recorded labeled/ inputs therefore came from code that is not in the notebook version under review. This corrects the scouts' earlier 'label mapping verified consistent' claim; the constant-Neutral identity is scoped to the recorded cell-32 vectors.

findings.title: A seeded, session-grouped, disjoint split is the minimal evidence-adoptable fix and it satisfies the contract the current code fails
findings.evidence: On integer inputs N=0..1000 the cell-37 construction passes 6/1001 cases (only N=0..5, where test is empty) and fails pairwise disjointness 995 times and session-group integrity 995 times (all N>=6). The retained replacement - whole groups from cell 27's subject/session metadata, shuffled with a fixed seed, assigned at 60/20/20, with a disjointness-and-coverage assertion - passes 1001/1001. At N=576 it yields 348/120/108 (60.42%/20.83%/18.75%), is bit-identical on repeated calls with the same seed, and differs under seed=7. Best-of-5 wall clock at n=100000: 1.923 ms (parent) vs 8.439 ms (replacement), both under 10 ms. Nothing was executed in the notebook and no accuracy was measured; the recorded 24.35% is not reproducible from this repository because the SEED-V data is absent.
